lesson.grammar_point: indefinite pronouns (somebody, anybody, nobody, everybody; something, anything, nothing, everything): some- in positive sentences, any- in questions and negatives, no- with a positive verb, every- with a singular verb

listenings.text: Good morning again, everybody, and thanks for waiting. Something was wrong with the scoreboard, but everything is fine now. Here are the results of heat two. It was a strange heat. For the first ten minutes, nobody caught anything. The ocean was completely flat. Then the sets came. In first place, with fourteen points, Jack Moore from Margaret River. And in second place, with a wave in the last twenty seconds, Renato Lara from Perth, with twelve point five. Is anybody here from the Perth squad? Yes, I can hear you! Both surfers go through to tomorrow's final. Renato, please come to the tent for a quick interview.

Renato, it's Dana. I'm sorry I wasn't at the tent with you. Somebody from the club needed help with the van. What a relief! When the scoreboard changed, I hugged everybody near me, even people I don't know! Listen. You didn't do anything wrong today. You waited, and you didn't waste anything. Tonight there's nothing to prepare. Just eat something good and rest. The final is tomorrow at ten. There are only four surfers in it, and everybody is good. But you deserve to be there. See you at the campsite.

items.situation: Jess arrives late and asks: "Did anybody catch a wave in the first ten minutes?" Answer her.
You come out of the water. Ask Kai if he filmed your last wave.
Tom asks: "What did you hear out there? The crowd was so loud!" Answer him.
Bev calls and asks: "Who was at the beach to watch you?" All the squad was there. Tell her.
Your teacher asks about a real day in your life when nothing worked at first, and then something changed. Tell the story in three sentences.
